requirement: Describe a prospective pilot randomized parallel comparison of ten weekly remote group sessions of Reward Re-Training versus active-control supportive group therapy in adults with bulimia nervosa or binge-eating disorder.

evidence.text: The protocol defines the two 10-session videoconference group conditions, target population and pilot RCT.

requirement: Specify or request confirmation of the random-allocation method, allocation concealment, group or therapist clustering constraints, and masking roles; do not infer these operational details from the word randomized.

evidence.text: The protocol states randomization and blinded assessors but does not define sequence generation, concealment or group-level constraints.

requirement: Use baseline, mid-treatment after session 5, post-treatment after session 10, and three-month post-treatment follow-up as the four longitudinal assessment times.

evidence.text: The assessment schedule specifies baseline, mid-treatment, post-treatment and three-month follow-up.
The SAP models all four time points.

requirement: Define the primary clinical outcomes as Eating Disorder Examination binge-eating frequency over the prior 28 days and EDE global eating-pathology score, assessed longitudinally.

evidence.text: The protocol identifies binge episodes and EDE global score as primary outcomes.
Primary Aim 3 models percent binge-frequency reduction and percent EDE-global change.

requirement: Define remission after baseline as no binge episodes or compensatory behaviors in the prior 28 days together with EDE global score below 1.74.

evidence.text: The protocol supplies the conjunctive remission definition.

requirement: Analyze depression, substance use, and quality of life as secondary outcomes using BDI-II, NIDA-modified ASSIST, and QOLI measurements across the four assessment times.

evidence.text: The protocol lists depression, substance use and quality of life and names their instruments.
Secondary Aim 1 applies the Primary Aim 3 approach to these outcomes.

requirement: Treat reward response to palatable food, reward or pleasure from day-to-day activities, social isolation, and loneliness as hypothesized target-engagement outcomes.

evidence.text: Primary Aim 2 and the assessment section define the four target domains and instruments.
The SAP plans separate longitudinal target models.

requirement: Prespecify feasibility and acceptability benchmarks of enrolling 60 participants, retaining more than 75% through all assessments, attendance at least 90% of treatment groups, and high satisfaction on feedback questionnaires.

evidence.text: Primary Aim 1 states the four benchmarks.

requirement: Produce descriptive summaries and exploratory graphs at each time point for the combined sample and by treatment; consider Box-Cox transformation when needed.

evidence.text: The opening statistical-design paragraph specifies summaries, graphs and transformation.

requirement: Compare baseline continuous variables by ANOVA or Kruskal-Wallis as appropriate and categorical variables by chi-square, and consider important arm imbalances as covariates.

evidence.text: The SAP defines baseline comparison and imbalance handling.

requirement: For each target-engagement outcome, fit a multilevel longitudinal model with baseline as time zero, treatment predicting individual intercept and slope, and a time-by-treatment interaction; estimate by REML in PROC MIXED.

evidence.text: Primary Aim 2 defines the two-level model and estimation.

requirement: Evaluate linear and higher-order time trends using AIC or BIC and report fitted-model contrasts at mid-treatment, post-treatment, and three-month follow-up.

evidence.text: Primary Aim 2 prespecifies model-selection criteria and three post-baseline contrasts.

requirement: Analyze percent reduction in binge frequency and percent change in EDE global pathology jointly over time with linear mixed-effects models including treatment, time, treatment-by-time, demographic and baseline-outcome fixed effects and subject and time random effects.

evidence.text: Primary Aim 3 defines the outcomes and fixed/random model terms.

requirement: Model therapist and participant-within-therapist variation separately, and use a common-within-arm exponential variance function plus continuous-time AR(1) residual correlation for unequal follow-up intervals.

evidence.text: Primary Aim 3 specifies variance components, heteroscedasticity and autocorrelation structures.

requirement: For mediation, test whether baseline-to-mid-treatment target change predicts post-treatment outcomes and post-treatment target change predicts three-month outcomes; estimate total and mediator-specific indirect effects with bias-corrected bootstrap inference.

evidence.text: The mediation paragraph defines temporal ordering and bootstrap indirect-effect testing.

requirement: Examine missing-data patterns, use likelihood-based estimation and multiple imputation, assess dropout influence with a Hedeker-Gibbons procedure, and perform sensitivity analyses when missingness may depend on the missing outcome.

evidence.text: The Attrition section states these missing-data analyses.

requirement: State the prospective pilot target as 60 participants, 30 per condition; distinguish this target from the 154 total needed for 80% power to detect a medium four-time-point mixed-model effect at alpha 0.05 and the 72 needed for a medium simple mediation effect.

evidence.text: The protocol plans 60 participants, 30 per condition.
The power section gives the 154 and 72 benchmarks and n=60 limitation.

requirement: Frame efficacy comparisons as preliminary effect-size estimation: with n=60 the study is powered only for large effects and may be underpowered for formal significance tests against active supportive therapy.

evidence.text: Primary Aim 3 is explicitly preliminary efficacy estimation.
The SAP states that n=60 detects large effects and interpretation will rely on effect sizes when underpowered.

requirement: Define the randomized analysis population and treatment attribution, including whether all randomized participants are retained under intention-to-treat and how participants with no post-baseline data are handled.

evidence.text: The protocol defines randomization and follow-up but no analysis set or attribution rule.
The SAP models longitudinal outcomes without naming an analysis population.

requirement: Define the denominator and fallback for percent binge-frequency reduction and percent EDE-global change when a baseline value is zero or near zero; do not leave percent-change outcomes mathematically undefined.

evidence.text: The SAP names percent-change outcomes without defining zero-baseline handling.

requirement: Declare whether feasibility, two clinical outcomes, remission, four target models, three secondary outcomes, time contrasts and mediation tests are exploratory or subject to multiplicity control; do not imply familywise control from nominal tests.

evidence.text: The protocol defines multiple aims, outcomes and targets without a hierarchy.
The plan specifies many models and contrasts but no multiplicity procedure.

requirement: Map remission and compensatory-behavior outcomes to explicit models, effect measures and confidence intervals, and clarify whether analyzing each condition separately is descriptive only or secondary to the randomized between-arm interaction.

evidence.text: The protocol defines remission and compensatory behaviors.
The plan specifies separate-condition examination but does not map binary outcomes or inference.
